title: routine-scheduler catalog
description: The components this console needs that the A2UI Basic Catalog has no equivalent for. It EXTENDS basic rather than replacing it (D310, the operator's answer a-rich-plus, 2026-11-23): a surface's default catalogId stays the basic catalog, and a component reaches these by naming this catalogId in its own @catalogId — which is how the protocol spells mixable catalogs. Nothing here duplicates a basic component: a decision's prose is basic Text, its options are a basic ChoicePicker, its submit is a basic Button. These three are the surfaces a general catalog cannot carry, because they render this system's own artefacts.
instructions:
Use the Basic Catalog for everything it covers — text, layout, inputs, buttons, cards, tabs, modals. Reach for a component here only when the thing being shown IS one of this system's artefacts:

- `RunTranscript` when the point is what a run DID: it renders turns as action/observation pairs with their own narration, which no arrangement of Text and Column reproduces readably.
- `DiffView` when the point is a CHANGE to a file: a unified diff with per-line gutters, so a reader can see what a patch would do before approving it.
- `GateVerdict` when the point is whether a candidate PASSED: the stages, their seconds and the failures, as one block that is scannable at a glance.

Every one of them takes its content from the data model by binding, never inline — the payloads are large and are updated by `updateDataModel` as a run progresses. Give each an `@accessibility.label` naming what it shows ('the gate verdict for 0.600.0'), because none of the three has a visible title of its own.

RunTranscript.description: One run's turns, as the console renders them: each turn an action with its narration and the observation that came back. Bound to an array in the data model, because a transcript grows while it is being watched.

turns.description: An array of turn objects, each with `turn` (number), `say` (string), `kind` (string) and optionally `observation` (string) and `usage` (object). Bind it with {"@path": …}: a transcript is large and is replaced by updateDataModel as the run proceeds.

runId.description: The run this transcript belongs to, shown as its heading and used as the link target when `linkable` is true.

linkable.description: Whether the heading links to the run's own page. False inside a surface that is itself shown on that page.

collapsed.description: Whether the turns start folded, leaving only the heading and the turn count. Use it when the transcript is context rather than the subject.

DiffView.description: A unified diff of one file, with per-line gutters — what a change WOULD do, rendered so a reader can approve or decline it on sight. The protocol's Text would show the same characters without the structure that makes a diff legible.

patch.description: The unified diff as text, one file's worth. Bind it rather than inlining it: a patch is large, and inlining it makes the component message grow with the change.

path.description: The file the patch applies to, shown as the diff's heading.

wrap.description: Whether long lines wrap instead of scrolling horizontally. Wrapping reads better in prose, scrolling preserves column alignment in code.

GateVerdict.description: Whether a candidate passed its gate, as one scannable block: the verdict, each stage with its seconds, and the failures by name. A general catalog has no component for this because the shape is this system's own.

verdict.description: green, red, timeout or running — the one word a reader needs first.

stages.description: An array of stage objects, each with `stage` (string), `seconds` (number), `exit_code` (number) and `failed` (array of node ids).

stamp.description: The gate stamp, so a verdict can be traced back to its evidence log.

action.description: Optional: what a click on the verdict dispatches — opening the evidence, or re-arming a stage.

format_duration.description: Seconds as the console spells a duration (`4m 12s`, `0.6s`), so a gate's stage times and a run's elapsed time read the same everywhere.

format_version.description: A release version as the console shows it, so an agent never has to spell the convention itself.
